svg.font-family: -apple-system, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: The electronics sled: front and back
The one removable plate that carries the screen, the boards and the battery. Drawn to scale: 2.5 px = 1 mm.
Front face: the side that looks out of the window
strip of thin double-sided tape, behind the glass
border above the picture: 4.7 mm (0.19 in)
border below the picture: 10.5 mm (0.41 in)
Glass, 0.91 mm thick, lies on the flat face,
held by the tape only: nothing clamps it.
No rim along the top or bottom.
Ribbon cable: 25.5 mm (1.00 in) wide, starting 72.2 mm (2.84 in) from the
glass's left edge. It folds back through the cut-out (dashed) to the back.
Back face: seen from behind, so the truck's rear is on the right
Hatched: the 2.5 mm strip at each end slides in the
Printed pocket and soft strap: 1 mm clear all round so
the battery can swell. Never clamped, never near a screw.
Battery lead: two wires to the main board's battery plug
The main board overhangs the plate's
rear edge to reach the rear wall.
Eight-wire cable from the adapter to
the main board, kept as one tidy bundle
screen glass; blue line: picture area
slides in a U-channel: keep clear
Built and tested on the bench as one working unit; it drops into the truck from the top.
On the bench, lay it face up or sit it in a printed stand. Never stand it on the ribbon.
Board positions are route B's. Routes A and C use smaller boards in the same places.
The adapter is drawn at 47 x 32 mm, the passive adapter's size. Measure the one you have.
Before the battery's first plug-in, check that its red wire meets the board's + mark.
